quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if the path is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if the path is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you may proceed. Always check that the intersection is clear. Let any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: Which of these is illegal?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass in no passing zones, on hills, in curves, or where you cannot see far ahead. You cannot pass at railroad crossings, street crossings, or in work zones where it is unsafe.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: When stopped by police, what documents must you show?
questions.explanation: You must have and show your driver's license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance when stopped by police or at a vehicle check.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways.
Only drive between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing a seat belt is the most important thing you can do to protect yourself in a crash.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you check?

options.text: Your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Check both mirrors to see traffic behind you. Then look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: If another driver is acting angry, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stay calm and avoid the angry driver. Don't make eye contact or hand gestures. Slow down, move away, or do whatever you can to stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do at a yield sign?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let other traffic enter the intersection first. You don't always have to stop, but you must give other traffic the right-of-way.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Only the alcohol's effect becomes weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug makes both stronger. For example, one drink taken with cold medicine can affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A person involved with a traffic study.

questions.explanation: You must always give the right-of-way to a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?
questions.explanation: Cold showers, black coffee, and exercise do not lower blood alcohol content. Only time will lower your BAC.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: The number of passengers in their car.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of aggression, such as unsafe lane changes. Do not challenge an aggressive driver. Instead, stay out of their way.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off the moisture and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: To avoid sudden stops:

options.text: Look ahead for hazards on the road.
Drive with your window partly down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead for hazards on the road.
questions.explanation: Watch ahead of your vehicle for hazards. If you have time to react, you are less likely to need a sudden stop or turn.

questions.question: If you see animals near the roadway while driving:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see animals near the road. They may run into traffic without warning. There may also be more animals nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Alcohol is the leading cause of fatal car crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the number one killer on American roads. It affects vision and slows reaction time. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your driving ability.

questions.question: Alcohol and drugs affect which driving skills?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm alertness, coordination, reaction time, and concentration—all needed for safe driving.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves ahead.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights?

options.text: Drive around the crossing gates if you don't see a train.
Stop completely behind the gates. Wait until the tracks are clear and the gates are raised before proceeding.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely behind the gates. Wait until the tracks are clear and the gates are raised before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when warning signs, flashing lights, or flaggers indicate a train is coming. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What should you do when you hear a fire engine siren behind you?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair driving. These include all alcoholic drinks, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many medicines (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: What is the problem with tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear)?

options.text: It can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
It cannot result in a traffic ticket.
It prevents being cut off and reduces collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is a behavior that leads to aggressive driving and should be avoided. Drivers can face legal consequences for unsafe driving.

questions.question: If you have an argument with someone and feel angry, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you don't think about the argument.
Wait a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the interstate to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your ability to drive safely. If you are very angry, excited, afraid, worried, or sad, wait until you are calm before driving. You need to focus mentally on driving without thinking about things that upset you.

questions.question: When is passing prohibited?

options.text: Within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
If the vehicle you are following has a slow-moving vehicle symbol.
When using the right lane to pass a left-turning vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass any vehicle within 100 feet of a railroad crossing or intersection. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: How do smoking and preparing to smoke affect driving?

options.text: They do not affect driving abilities.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready for yellow, red, and green lights, and watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: How can road rage and aggressive driving be reduced?
questions.explanation: As more drivers use the roads, road rage increases. To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.
Wait until the person crosses the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way at all times. You must wait for them to cross.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt together. Using only one part does not protect you as well. Even if you have an automatic shoulder belt, you must also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the car straight and slow down gradually by letting off the gas pedal.
Keep your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down gradually by letting off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car going straight. Release the gas pedal slowly and do not brake until you have full control. Once the car is stable, brake gently and move to the nearest safe spot off the road.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to a safe speed for the turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows rules drivers must follow. This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: Drivers should keep a safe distance from cyclists.
questions.explanation: Drivers must be careful around cyclists and keep a safe distance between their vehicle and the cyclist.
